title: Certificates of Deposit: Booking the Renewal That Falls Owed When Grace Ends
content:
A Certificate of Deposit that is set to renew does not stop at the end of its grace period: on the day after grace ends, if nothing done during grace has closed it, it moves into a new term. This page covers how Piedmont Crescent Bank books that new term on its Certificates of Deposit and prices it, and the tool used to record it.

## What is governed

The renewal is owed by the bank on the strength of the certificate's own record, whether or not the owner calls. Booking it sets the certificate back to active status in its new term, fixes the new term's dates, its interest rate and APY, and records whether each of the two bonuses forms part of the new rate. Its principal is left as it stands.

## The booking tool

`renew_certificate_term_21cb639a` is an agent tool that stays hidden until unlocked. The agent unlocks it by passing its name to `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then invokes it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Effect of a call.** The certificate starts its next term: it becomes active again in the tier given, carrying the new term start date and maturity date, the rate and APY fixed for the new term, and the two bonus markers for that term. The one bump-up allowed per term becomes available again, and the renewal count rises by one. The principal balance is untouched. The new term appears on the certificate record at once.

**Parameters.**

| Name | Meaning | Format and permitted values |
|---|---|---|
| `certificate_id` | the certificate being renewed, from the certificate lookup for this customer | certificate reference number |
| `variant_name` | the tier of the new term | one of `6-Month Certificate`, `11-Month No-Penalty Certificate`, `12-Month Certificate`, `18-Month Bump-Up Certificate`, `36-Month Certificate`, `60-Month Certificate` |
| `term_start_date` | the first day of the new term | calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD, never empty |
| `maturity_date` | the day the new term matures | calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD, never empty |
| `interest_rate` | the new term's annual interest rate with bonuses included | a number of percent, to 2 decimal places |
| `apy` | the new term's annual percentage yield with bonuses included | a number of percent, to 2 decimal places |
| `jumbo_bonus_applied` | whether the Jumbo Bonus is part of the new rate | `true` (included) or `false` (not included) |
| `relationship_bonus_applied` | whether the Relationship Bonus is part of the new rate | `true` (included) or `false` (not included) |

**Receipt.** A successful call returns `certificate_id`, `status` (active), `variant_name`, `term_start_date` and `maturity_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `interest_rate` and `apy` (percent, 2 decimal places), `jumbo_bonus_applied` and `relationship_bonus_applied` (true or false), and `renewal_count` (the renewal count after this renewal, a whole number). A receipt showing status active means the new term is booked.

## Basis Q&A

**Does booking the new term move any money?** No. The tool records the term; the principal balance is not changed by it.

**Does the tool work out the rate?** No. It records the dates, rate, APY and markers it is given.
